title: Texas blues singers, Charlie Dixon and Bessie Smith
summary: Albert says Texas blues singers did not sing opera and praises Charlie Dixon as a great man and bassist.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Yeah, he never did talk much about them until I got to know him well. Which I was especially close to him. And Willie Tyson, did you ever know him? A piano player?
Yeah, that man rings a bell, but I've forgotten what you talked about. Yes.
I've listened to a lot of these guys singing blues from Texas. Men. Like Kellogg Jefferson and all that.
Did they sing opera too? No.
They never were that style of singing.
They, they, they only singers that possibly if opera came up and sung would be Ed Sanders and Mickie Johnson. Wow.
Now what about, uh, Charlie Dixon? Who all did they, they were.

Charlie Dixon was one of the greatest men that I've met in my life. I wouldn't say he was the greatest musician, but he was truly a great man. And by the same token, he could play his bass and he could play his punk. He played with Singers Smith, which was another band that I didn't know, but Brad's room, Brad's first day. Charlie Dixon was a good band. Charlie Dixon was a good band. In fact, if it, uh, in fact if it wasn't for him, uh, I think Troy's family had broken up on one time for a year.
But, did he record with anybody or other than Troy?

Yeah, he recorded, uh, with, uh, with, uh, with, uh, with, uh, with a few other individuals. And, uh, Sugaroo and, uh, was a part of the other side. Charlie recorded with them. Uh-huh. Sometimes on the tuba, sometimes on the drum.
Now what about Betsy Smith? Did he ever play with her again?
I, I doubt seriously. Betsy Smith doesn't come around this area. I see.
